html:
A long poem in Old Javanese that retells the Indian epic Ramayana, written in central Java in the late 9th or early 10th century. It is the oldest surviving kakawin, the Javanese form of court poetry built on Sanskrit metres.

It was composed in the time of the kingdom of Mataram, the same period when the story was carved at Prambanan. Its translator Stuart Robson dates it between 856 and 930. The poet did not follow Valmiki directly but the Sanskrit Bhattikavya, a learned version of the tale, and then went his own way, adding long scenes of nature and advice on good kingship.

The poem became a classic. It is still recited in Bali, and its version of the story shaped the shadow puppet theatre of wayang in Java and Bali. Together with the Prambanan reliefs, it shows how Indian stories were made Javanese.
